title: I killed my Polymarket BTC bot a while ago. Somehow Orphis is alive again.
author: Orphis_
selftext:
A while back I posted about Orphis, my attempt at building a bot around Polymarket's BTC 15-minute Up/Down markets.

Then I basically **stopped**.

The project was getting way too big, I was burning through AI subscriptions/tokens, and what started as "lol let's make a trading bot" had turned into me arguing with edge cases at 3am.

Well... **Orphis** is alive again.

And this time I rebuilt the whole thing with a very different mindset.

I'm not trying to rush a strategy into production anymore. The goal now is to build the boring infrastructure properly first:

\- 24/7 BTC 15m market recording

\- Polymarket order book + trades

\- Chainlink + Binance reference prices

\- deterministic replay

\- data quality checks

\- crash/reconnect handling

\- storage/archive system

\- eventually proper backtesting → paper trading → tiny live capital



The recorder has now been running continuously on a separate Ubuntu machine and the project has gotten **way** more serious than I originally intended.

Today I also successfully archived the first real production data segment **losslessly** compressed \~60 MB → \~2.8 MB, deleted the hot copy, replayed it from the archive, and got the exact same hashes / event counts / QA results.

Which is an absurd milestone considering this project originally started as me trying to make a quick Polymarket bot.

Still **zero claims of profitability**. I haven't even reached the part where I seriously test whether an edge exists yet.

Right now I'm just trying to make sure the research infrastructure can't quietly lie to me.

I'll put the unnecessarily detailed technical status in a comment because nobody wants that wall of text in the post lol.

comments.author: Orphis_
comments.body:
Small technical update for anyone following the project:



The current version is much more of a research/trading infrastructure project than the original bot.

Current status:

\- 24/7 BTC 15m market recorder is running

\- Polymarket + external BTC reference data is being collected

\- raw data and normalized events are stored separately

\- recorded sessions can be deterministically replayed

\- data integrity / freshness / gap checks are automated

\- reconnects, crashes and market rollovers are handled

\- hot/cold storage is now working

\- current test suite: 300 passing tests



The storage work became a project by itself because the recorder produces 3+ GB/hour.   
  
The first real production archive test compressed a 59.9 MB segment to 2.78 MB, around 21.5x smaller, while preserving the exact original data. I've also been deliberately holding back automatic archival because adversarial testing kept finding increasingly cursed edge cases involving locks, processes and files being deleted while still open.



I'd rather have the system refuse to do something than quietly corrupt the dataset.

Next milestone is the part I've been waiting for:

backtester → baseline strategies → actual signal research → paper trading.  


I still have no idea whether the BTC 15m market has an exploitable edge.

That's kind of the point now.



I want the infrastructure trustworthy enough that if the answer is "no edge", I can actually believe it.

comments.author: Emotional-Breath-838
comments.body:
Bots do research well. 

I’ve yet to see bots trade well.

replies.author: Orphis_
replies.body: True that. I hope things work out in the next couple of months.
